Garden City.wildlife_intro:
Garden City is Nassau's planned cathedral village — a 19th-century planned community of uniform, gracious streets, hedged lots, and the Cathedral of the Incarnation at its center, where the landscaping itself is the wildlife habitat. Squirrels work the village's formal canopy into attics, and moles are the signature Garden City complaint: the village's irrigated, immaculate lawns are perfect mole ground, and a single mole can ridge a showcase front yard in a week. Our crew inspects Garden City homes roof to lawn, removes the animals, seals the entries, and treats the mole work as its own craft: reading tunnel systems and placing effort where the active runs actually are, rather than scattering it across the whole yard.
